To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LiMn2 and CuM2O4 spinel materials have been synthesized by Pechinni method.
LiMn2 and CuMm2 spinels are promising candidates for thermochemical heat storage due to the reversibility of the redox processes, the high enthalpy values, and the high cycling stability.
the thermochemical heat energy storage properties of LiMn2X4 and CuM2O4 (X=O and X=O2) spinel oxides have been studied for the first time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the thermochemical heat capacity of two spinels: CuMn2 O4 and LiM n2 O4.
the study of the thermochemical properties of CuMn 2O 4 and LiM 2O 2 spinels for thermochemical energy conversion.
the study of two mixed oxides with spinel structure (CuMn2O2 and LiMn4) as potential thermochemical materials for high temperature energy storage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CuMn2 O4 and LiM n 2 O4 are stable materials with a high heat storage capacity, but the reduction and oxidation temperatures must be adjusted to obtain the highest values.
the use of Li and Cu cations in Mn2O4 spinel is a viable strategy for the development of new materials for high temperature thermochemistry.
the use of a reducing atmosphere in thermochemical heat storage is an interesting alternative that should be considered in order to improve the performance of the redox materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the first time, the heat storage potential of CuMn 2O4 and its redox mechanism has been studied, and the obtained results are comparable with the ones obtained for LiMn 2 O4.
the redox reactions between CuMn2 O4 and LiM n2 O4 with air and argon at temperatures between 700 and 1000 °C are feasible for heat storage applications.
the use of Li or Cu cations to form mixed manganese oxides is a promising approach to develop materials for thermochemical heat storage.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a suitable atmosphere in the redox reactions can be a powerful tool to improve the thermochemical heat capacity of the material, and therefore, to optimize the heat storage capacity of redox systems.

the enthalpy of redox transformations of these oxides is significantly higher if the re-oxidization takes place in air, and this is a promising approach for increasing the heat storage capacity of redox materials.
it is possible to tune the redox properties of the materials by varying the composition of the reaction atmosphere.
